title: Slot0 price manipulation + zero-slippage liquidity removal enables direct WETH extraction from AerodromeAMO

actors.name: strategist
actors.role: Broadcasts rebalance transaction visible in mempool

actors.name: amo_contract
actors.role: AerodromeAMO holding WETH in LP position

steps.action: Establish baseline pool state with 1:1 WETH:OETHb reserves at normal slot0 sqrtPriceX96
Simulate Phase 1 (FL-003): attacker manipulates slot0 sqrtPriceX96 by 2x (doubling price) before strategist's rebalance mint call
steps.expected_result: Manipulated price causes AerodromeAMO to calculate inflated OETHb mint amount using slot0 spot price instead of TWAP

steps.action: Compute oethb_minted_normal vs oethb_minted_manipulated using the buggy get_mint_amount logic that reads slot0 directly
Simulate Phase 2 (FL-006): with pool already OETHb-heavy, strategist calls _removeLiquidity with zero slippage (min_amounts = 0). Attacker sandwiches the tx.
steps.expected_result: Because pool is skewed toward OETHb, removing LP shares yields proportionally less WETH than expected at fair price. Attacker front-runs to push price further, back-runs to capture WETH.

steps.action: Verify _solvencyAssert cannot detect imbalance: it checks oethb_supply against a fixed parity constant (1e18) rather than spot price from pool
steps.expected_result: _solvencyAssert passes even when pool is heavily imbalanced because parity_check = oethb_supply / PARITY_CONSTANT does not use pool reserves or slot0

steps.action: Calculate WETH shortfall for withdrawal queue: weth_received_fair - weth_received_manipulated
steps.expected_result: Positive WETH shortfall demonstrating direct fund loss from vault withdrawal queue

assertions.expected_correct_value: oethb_minted_normal (1x fair amount based on reserves)
assertions.reason: get_mint_amount reads slot0.sqrtPriceX96 directly without TWAP validation, so a 2x price manipulation causes 2x OETHb over-mint
Zero slippage (min_amounts=0) allows removal at any price, and pool already skewed OETHb-heavy due to Phase 1, so WETH received is less than fair share
_solvencyAssert uses fixed PARITY_CONSTANT (1e18) not pool spot price, so OETHb over-supply is invisible to the check
Chained exploit: Phase 1 reduces cost of Phase 2 attack; combined they extract WETH from withdrawal queue

failure_modes: Compile errors if Soroban-specific integer types are required but standard Rust u128/i128 are used instead
The actual slot0 reading logic or mint amount formula may differ from what is reconstructed from the description, requiring source code access to copy verbatim
The _solvencyAssert logic may use a different comparison than assumed; if it does check spot price the assertion about it passing would be wrong
The exact sqrtPriceX96 to token amount conversion formula (using Q96 fixed point) may have subtle differences from the Aerodrome implementation
If the bug has already been patched (e.g., TWAP added or slippage parameter enforced), the test would demonstrate the fixed behavior instead
The chained nature means Phase 2 profit depends on exact Phase 1 parameters; off-by-one in reserve math could make the shortfall zero in pure arithmetic
